To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the decision to out-source IS/IT is not related to the performance of the IS/IT department, but it is related to the firm's competitive strategy; (2) the decision to outsourcing is not a cost reduction strategy; (3) the decision to use an IS/IT outsourcing strategy is related to the creation, maintenance, and development of resources that provide a competitive advantage to the firm.
The decision to outsource is related to the creation or improvement of valuable resources and market transaction costs, while the IS/IT performance does not influence this decision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors determining outsourcing in the IS/IT activity of a hotel, from the resource-based perspective.
the factors affecting the outsourcing of IS/IT activities and the reasons that justify this strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors affecting outsourcing are the same in both the strategic and the tactical areas, although the reasons justifying the outsourcing strategy are different.

outsourcing is a strategic decision, which is based on the firm’s core competencies, and the outsourcing of IS/IT activities is justified by the need to improve the quality of the service and concentrate on the firm’s strategic activities.
the decision to out-source is not a simple one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
outsourcing of IS/IT activities is a strategic decision and that the factors that influence this decision are the same as those for any other outsourcing decision.

outsourcing of IS/IT activities in hotels is not a decision taken only to cut costs, but rather a strategic decision to improve the quality of service, to concentrate resources in the core activities and to obtain the best resources in the market.
the outsourcing decisions are made based on strategic reasons.

the factors determining IS outsourcing are related to resource creation, market transaction costs and the quality of the IS/IT service.
